tenders.title: S30168 Feasibility study for developing a quality measure for variable signs and signals settings
tenders.summary: Timeliness of variable signs and signals (VSS) settings is one of our company's performance indicators. However, we're not able to evaluate the quality of these settings, whether they're appropriate a
tenders.detailedDescription: Timeliness of variable signs and signals (VSS) settings is one of our company's performance indicators. However, we're not able to evaluate the quality of these settings, whether they're appropriate and beneficial for those using our roads. These factors drive customer trust and satisfaction and influence both the Strategic Roads User Survey (SRUS) and Average Delay Key Performance Indicator scores. A KPMG review of our SRUS performance recommended measuring the quality of VSS settings to help identify how we can improve scores. As part of our CSC Business Plan requirement to improve customer experience through better in-journey information we want to commit £83,289.85 of funding (approved through a portfolio business case for VSS improvements by CSC IDC) to carry out a feasibility study to explore the potential of developing a VSS quality measure that would give us sight of how well we're doing in this area. This work is part of the Customer Service Development Group's ongoing portfolio of VSS improvements which seek to improve customer experience and contribute to an increase in customer satisfaction scores. In the 2025-26 reporting year SRUS recorded 71% overall satisfaction and 69% for information on electronic signs. The RIS3 KPI requires SRUS scores to improve year-on-year. Any proposed measure should aim at helping us to identify where changes can improve satisfaction scores. We anticipate the feasibility study will require engagement with National Highways' teams to draw expertise and input on the potential of existing system and process outputs to be used to assess the quality of settings made. Therefore, some travel may be required. National Highways will facilitate the consultant's access to contributing teams. This feasibility study involves no additional IT or resource requirements.
